newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RELEGATED MIDDLESBROUGH LOOKING FOR FINAL GLORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RELEGATED MIDDLESBROUGH LOOKING FOR FINAL GLORY.

text.p: Middlesbrough may be down and out of the English premier league, but their season could still end in bitter-sweet glory if they win the F.A. Cup for the first time next Saturday.
Any celebration would be somewhat muted because their failure to avoid the drop into the first division will be felt for months, and possibly years to come.

And victory in the cup final -- as well as a possible legal challenge against their relegation through the courts -- will also determine whether their foreign players like Juninho, Emerson, Fabrizio Ravanelli and Gianluca Festa stay at the club.
The chances are that they could all leave even if Middlesbrough do beat Chelsea and win the cup to claim their first major trophy in their 121-year history.
But like just about everything that has happened to Middlesbrough this season, the situation is far from clear-cut.

Middlesbrough went down not because they had one of the three worst playing records over the season, but because they had three points deducted for refusing to play a match at Blackburn on December 21 because they claimed they had more than 20 players out through injury and illness.

They were subsequently docked three points for refusing to play the fixture at the time and had an appeal against the deduction turned down. If they had played the match and not lost the points they would have finished 14th and safe. Instead, they came 19th.
Chairman Steve Gibson did not rule out the possibility of legal action after Sunday's 1-1 draw at Leeds sealed relegation.
Asked on Sky TV whether the club would pursue the issue, and throw the premier league and first division into chaos, Gibson said: "I will do what is right for Middlesbrough Football Club.
"We have been relegated today not because of what happened on the football pitch but because of a decision made by grey men in grey suits behind closed doors."
Asked whether a legal challenge would be made, Gibson replied: "That's for me to know. Those who deducted us three points will be the first to know my message."
He added: "The determination of the club to achieve our objectives are still here. We were hopeful for today but it has not happened."
So Middlesbrough, who lost the League Cup final to Leicester in April after a replay, now return to Wembley in confusing circumstances.
Bryan Robson, who spent 16 million pounds ($26 million) assembling his team of highly paid foreigners, now has the task of motivating them after the shattering disappointment of relegation.
"The players are all very quiet in the dressing room but we can't do anything about being relegated now," he said.
"I have told them that they've got to start preparing themselves tonight for the cup final. It won't make up for relegation if we win it but it will be a great way to finish the season."
Robson refused to comment on his future at the club, or that of any of the players.
But Middlesbrough looked exhausted as they ended their fourth match in nine days, crushed by the realisation they had gone down, upset by the sight of so many fans openly weeping.
At least they now have almost a week to rest and prepare for the cup final while Ravanelli, who was unfit for Sunday's match, should be fit to face Chelsea.

No English team have won the cup and been relegated in the same season. It would be perfectly in keeping with their schizophrenic season if that is exactly what baffling Middlesbrough achieve next weekend.
